summary: The article surveys five MLB teams with managerial vacancies after the 2023 season: the Angels, Astros, Guardians, Mets and Padres. For each team it explains why the job opened and lists possible candidates, noting factors like Shohei Ohtani's free agency, Cleveland's low payroll and David Stearns' ties to Craig Counsell. It closes by saying the teams will narrow their options before 2024.
one_line: Five MLB teams (Angels, Astros, Guardians, Mets, Padres) need new managers for 2024, and the article lists likely candidates for each.
key_facts: The Angels declined Phil Nevin's 2024 club option; he went 119-149 (.444) over parts of two seasons after taking over as interim manager for the final 106 games of 2022 when Joe Maddon was relieved.
The Angels' managerial outlook depends on Shohei Ohtani's decision, and the team has a playoff drought spanning 9 seasons plus a below-par farm system.
Possible Angels candidates named are Ray Montgomery, Walt Weiss, Ron Washington and Clayton McCullough.
Dusty Baker, 74, retired after his fourth season with the Astros and 26th big league managerial season; Houston won the 2022 World Series under him, then lost the 2023 ALCS to the Texas Rangers.

Astros candidates include Joe Espada (48, bench coach since 2018), Buck Showalter, Don Mattingly and A. J. Hinch; the Astros won six of the previous seven AL West titles, but Luis Garcia (Tommy John surgery) and Lance McCullers Jr. (forearm surgery) leave the rotation shaky.

Terry Francona resigned from the Guardians over health concerns after 11 years, a 921-757 record (.549), six playoff trips and the 2016 AL pennant, making him the winningest manager in franchise history.

Cleveland has one of baseball's lowest payrolls and is open to outside hires; candidates include Craig Albernaz (40, Giants catching and bullpen coach, interview slated) and Carlos Mendoza (43, Yankees bench coach).
Buck Showalter won 2022 NL Manager of the Year with a 101-61 Mets record, but the Mets finished 2023 at 75-87 despite baseball's largest budget.

New Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns, a former Brewer, has a strong relationship with Craig Counsell, whose Milwaukee Brewers contract is nearing its end; Gabe Kapler is another possibility.
Bob Melvin was expected to return to the Padres after an 82-80 season without a postseason berth, but the San Francisco Giants hired him after San Diego allowed them to interview him.

Bob Nightengale of USA Today Sports reports Mike Shildt is the favorite for the Padres job, with associate manager Ryan Flaherty also getting strong consideration; it will be A. J. Preller's sixth manager in 10 years.
